verses.1: The heads of the paternal families of the clan of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, from the clans of the sons of Joseph, came forward before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelites.
verses.2: They said, “Our lord, the Lord has commanded to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the Israelites, and our lord has been commanded by the Lord to give the inheritance of our brother Tzlofchad to his daughters.
verses.3: But if they marry into one of the tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestors and added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they go as wives, and from the lot of our inheritance it will be subtracted.
verses.4: And if the Jubilee occurs for the Israelites and their inheritance is added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they go as wives, then it will be subtracted from the inheritance of the tribe of our ancestors.”
verses.5: Moses gave an order to the Israelites by the command of the Lord, saying, “The tribe of the sons of Joseph is speaking rightly.
verses.6: This is the instruction the Lord has given regarding the daughters of Tzlofchad: ‘They may marry whom they please in their judgment, but they must marry within the clan of the tribe of their father’s family.
verses.7: No inheritance may pass from one tribe to another among the Israelites, for the Israelites must remain attached to the inheritance of their ancestral tribe.
verses.8: And every daughter who inherits an inheritance from the tribes of the Israelites must marry into the family of a man from her father’s tribe, so that the Israelites may each inherit the inheritance of their ancestors.
verses.9: No inheritance may pass from one tribe to another tribe, for the Israelites must remain attached to their own inheritance.”
verses.10: As the Lord had commanded Moses, so the daughters of Tzlofchad did.
verses.11: The daughters of Tzlofchad—Mahlah, Tirtzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah—married their father’s relatives, their uncle’s sons.
verses.12: They married into the clans of the sons of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the inheritance of the tribe of their father’s family.
verses.13: These are the decrees and judgments that the Lord gave by the hand of Moses to the Israelites in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: “will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestors” — the Hebrew uses the root נָשַׁב (nashav), which can mean “taken away” or “transferred,” and is used here in the legal sense of a change in inheritance rights.
- v. 6: “they may marry whom they please in their judgment” — the Hebrew uses לַטּוֹב בְּעֵינֵיהֶם (latov be-einayhem), literally “the good in their eyes,” which conveys their right to choose a spouse.
- v. 12: “their uncle’s sons” — the Hebrew specifies that the daughters married their father’s relatives, specifically their father’s brothers’ sons, i.e., their uncles’ sons.
- v. 13: “the plains of Moab” — the Hebrew term עַרְבֹת מוֹאָב (arbot Moav) literally means “plains of Moab,” a well-established geographic designation.

[1] The heads of the paternal families of the clan of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, from the clans of the sons of Joseph, came forward before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelites.

[2] They said, “Our lord, the Lord has commanded to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the Israelites, and our lord has been commanded by the Lord to give the inheritance of our brother Tzlofchad to his daughters.

[3] But if they marry into one of the tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestors and added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they go as wives, and from the lot of our inheritance it will be subtracted.

[4] And if the Jubilee occurs for the Israelites and their inheritance is added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they go as wives, then it will be subtracted from the inheritance of the tribe of our ancestors.”

[5] Moses gave an order to the Israelites by the command of the Lord, saying, “The tribe of the sons of Joseph is speaking rightly.

[6] This is the instruction the Lord has given regarding the daughters of Tzlofchad: ‘They may marry whom they please in their judgment, but they must marry within the clan of the tribe of their father’s family.

[7] No inheritance may pass from one tribe to another among the Israelites, for the Israelites must remain attached to the inheritance of their ancestral tribe.

[8] And every daughter who inherits an inheritance from the tribes of the Israelites must marry into the family of a man from her father’s tribe, so that the Israelites may each inherit the inheritance of their ancestors.

[9] No inheritance may pass from one tribe to another tribe, for the Israelites must remain attached to their own inheritance.”

[10] As the Lord had commanded Moses, so the daughters of Tzlofchad did.

[11] The daughters of Tzlofchad—Mahlah, Tirtzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah—married their father’s relatives, their uncle’s sons.

[12] They married into the clans of the sons of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the inheritance of the tribe of their father’s family.

[13] These are the decrees and judgments that the Lord gave by the hand of Moses to the Israelites in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho.
